B. Is this measure already running in South Karelia wellbeing services county (or in the HUS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Fitness assessment and prehabilitation before deciding against curative treatment. Before a stage I-III patient is judged too frail, they get an exercise test, a geriatric assessment if over 75, and four weeks of supervised exercise, breathing training and help to stop smoking. Then the decision is made again.
effect_summary_en: A Cochrane review (2022, 10 RCTs, 636 participants) finds that exercise before lung surgery cuts lung complications after surgery (RR 0.45), but it does not measure how many more patients become fit for curative treatment.
supported_en: A Cochrane review (2022) finds that exercise before lung surgery cuts lung complications after surgery (risk ratio 0.45).
not_supported_en: No page I read measures an increase in the share of patients treated with curative intent, so the assumed 0.5 points is not shown.
summary_en: I found no public sign that this measure is running in South Karelia or at HUS. HUS patients booked for lung surgery meet a physiotherapist and are told how to prepare for the operation, and Ekhva's lung clinic has a stop-smoking nurse, but no page describes four weeks of supervised exercise followed by a second decision for patients judged too frail. On the effect, a Cochrane review (2022) finds that exercise before surgery cuts lung complications after surgery (risk ratio 0.45, meaning about 55% fewer), but it does not measure how many more patients become fit for surgery.
unanswered_en: I found no HUS or Ekhva page on supervised prehabilitation, exercise testing or geriatric assessment for patients judged too frail, followed by a second treatment decision.
